design_detail: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover in 10 men with recreational MDMA experience. Two sessions a week apart with a two-week washout: in one, placebo capsules at 9 a.m. and 100 mg MDMA two hours later; in the other, 50 mg MDMA at 9 a.m. and 100 mg MDMA two hours later. The comparison of interest is therefore the response to the same 100 mg dose with and without a 50 mg dose two hours earlier. All pharmacodynamic measures were expressed as change from the baseline before the first capsule, and both the peak effect and the area under the curve were taken over the window 2-6 hours, that is, after the 100 mg dose, with repeated-measures analyses of variance and post-hoc t tests at each time point. Plasma MDMA, MDA and the metabolites HMMA and HMA were measured to 50 hours, with compartmental modelling used to estimate the 50 mg dose's contribution to total exposure.
can_establish: Whether a 50 mg dose two hours earlier changes the plasma concentrations, metabolite pattern and acute response to a 100 mg dose of MDMA in the same men, at an interval the authors chose to resemble recreational redosing.
cannot_establish: What a second equal dose does (the two doses differed, 50 then 100 mg, so the design is not a repeat of the same dose); what happens after more than two doses or at larger doses; effects in women, who were not studied; and whether the smaller-than-expected responses are tolerance rather than ceiling effects, which the authors name as an alternative, or an artefact of the first dose's effects still being present when the second was given, which they also name.

sample.recruitment: Recruited from the surrounding community by word of mouth; the study was run at a hospital research institute in Barcelona (Materials and methods > Subjects, 1st paragraph, p. 884).
sample.inclusion_exclusion: Recreational experience of ecstasy on 5-50 occasions without serious adverse reaction, no abuse or dependence on other substances by DSM-IV criteria other than nicotine; general medical examination, psychiatric interview, laboratory tests, urinalysis and electrocardiogram to exclude medical or psychiatric conditions; only people phenotyped as extensive metabolizers of the enzyme that clears MDMA were included. Two further men took part in a pilot condition (50 plus 75 mg) whose data are not shown (p. 884).
sample.demographics: Ten men, mean age 24.9 years (range 22-35), weight 70.7 kg (range 57.5-81.6), height 177.7 cm (range 171-190). All had used cannabis, 83.3% cocaine, 75% LSD, 25% other amphetamines and 50% other substances such as ketamine or GHB; all but two smoked (under 20 cigarettes a day); average alcohol intake 9.4 units a week (range 1-25) (p. 884).
sample.attrition: None reported: all ten completed both sessions and the paper states that no participant needed specific treatment or special care.
sample.selection_effects: Men only, young, healthy, experienced with MDMA and selected to be fast metabolizers of it; people who metabolize it slowly, the group in whom accumulation would be greatest, were excluded by design, and women were not studied. The percentages of previous drug use (83.3%, 75%) do not correspond to whole numbers out of ten (see reporting issues).

exposure.measurement: Drug given in the laboratory in identical opaque capsules and measured directly: plasma MDMA, MDA, HMMA and HMA by gas chromatography-mass spectrometry at 18 time points from baseline to 50 hours after the first capsule (p. 886).
exposure.dose_frequency_duration_route: Study conditions only: oral racemic MDMA supplied by the Spanish Ministry of Health in 50 mg capsules. Session A: two placebo capsules at 9 a.m., then 100 mg (two active capsules) at 11 a.m. Session B: 50 mg (one active and one placebo capsule) at 9 a.m., then 100 mg at 11 a.m. (pp. 884-885).
exposure.polysubstance: Participants were asked to avoid psychoactive drugs for at least three days before and throughout the study and caffeine or alcohol for 48 hours before each session, with a urine screen for opiates, cocaine metabolite, amphetamines and cannabinoids on arrival; smoking was allowed only from 6 p.m. (pp. 884-885).
exposure.abstinence_at_testing: Overnight fast and a drug-free urine screen before each session; sessions once a week with a two-week washout between them. In the repeated-dose session, MDMA from the 50 mg dose was still present when the 100 mg dose was given: peak 84.71 ng/mL and 79.92 ng/mL at the 2-hour point (p. 889).

comparison.controls: Within-person: the same men received 100 mg alone (after placebo) and 100 mg preceded by 50 mg. There is no placebo-only session, so the 2-6 hour effects are compared between two active conditions rather than against placebo.
comparison.matching: Within-person randomized, double-blind crossover with a two-week washout.
comparison.unmeasured_premorbid: Not applicable: every comparison is within person.

outcomes.instruments: Systolic and diastolic blood pressure, heart rate, oral temperature and pupil diameter; digit-symbol substitution, simple reaction time, the Pauli test and the Maddox-wing device; 21 visual analogue scales and the 49-item short-form Addiction Research Center Inventory with five subscales; plasma concentrations of MDMA and three metabolites. Pharmacodynamic measures were taken at 16-17 time points to 26 hours (pp. 885-886).
outcomes.validity_norms: The laboratory's standard battery, used in its earlier MDMA studies; subjective scales have no external norms.
outcomes.operationalization: Tolerance is operationalized informally as effects after the second dose that are lower than the plasma concentrations would predict; no concentration-effect model is fitted, and 'expected' is judged against dose proportionality.
outcomes.multiplicity_correction: None at the family level: each variable was tested on peak, area under the curve and time course, with post-hoc t tests at each time point, at p<0.05 (p. 886).
outcomes.assessor_blinding: Double-blind with identical capsules; blinding integrity was not assessed, and participants with MDMA experience are likely to have detected the 50 mg dose, since its effects were measurable before the second capsule.

analysis.effect_sizes: Means with standard deviations are printed for every outcome in Table 1 (n=10, change from baseline over 2-6 hours) and for pharmacokinetic parameters in Tables 2 and 3. Key contrasts, single 100 mg against 50+100 mg: systolic pressure peak 29.50 (SD 9.69) against 33.30 (SD 4.13) mm Hg, not significant, with the area under the curve 49.35 (SD 24.28) against 72.96 (SD 22.12), p=0.029; diastolic peak 11.85 (SD 13.83) against 18.90 (SD 12.33), not significant, area under the curve 18.81 against 46.82, p=0.015; heart-rate peak 33.50 (SD 11.87) against 33.05 (SD 13.25) and area under the curve 57.75 against 69.98, both not significant; temperature peak 0.20 against 0.56 degrees Celsius and area under the curve 0.50 against 1.61, both not significant; pupil diameter peak 3.39 against 3.74 mm, not significant, area under the curve 9.42 against 11.92, p=0.037. Pharmacokinetics: peak MDMA concentration 202.92 ng/mL (SD 30.30) against 311.16 (SD 66.48), p<0.001; exposure to 50 hours 2890.73 against 4426.60 microgram.h/L; half-life 10.41 h (SD 3.55) against 10.48 (SD 2.12); the 50 mg dose contributed 0.30 (SD 0.01) of total exposure and the 100 mg dose 0.67 (SD 0.13). Against dose proportionality, peak concentration was 12.8% and exposure 16.2% higher than expected, while the metabolite HMMA was 38.2% lower at peak and 29.8% lower in exposure.
analysis.covariates: None; all measures expressed as change from the pre-first-capsule baseline.
analysis.preregistration_detail: No registration is mentioned; the protocol was approved by the local research ethics committee and authorized by the Spanish Ministry of Health (pp. 884-885).
analysis.selective_reporting: Table 1 shows only variables with a significant difference somewhere, so the wanted subjective effects (euphoria, liking, stimulation on the visual analogue scales) appear only as the statement that they did not differ; the pilot condition's data are not shown; figures carry no printed values.
analysis.power: No sample-size calculation. The authors state in their limitations that the sample size may limit the power to show differences, alongside ceiling effects on several scales.

interpretation_gap.results_show: Giving 50 mg two hours before a 100 mg dose raised peak MDMA concentration by about half (203 to 311 ng/mL) and exposure by about 50%, somewhat more than dose proportionality predicts (+12.8% peak, +16.2% exposure), while the metabolite HMMA fell well below proportionality, consistent with inhibition of MDMA's own metabolism. Blood pressure, temperature and pupil diameter were higher in the repeated-dose condition on the area under the curve or at scattered time points, whereas heart rate did not differ in peak or area under the curve, and none of the wanted subjective effects (euphoria, liking, stimulation) differed in peak or area; one perceptual scale was lower after the repeated dose.
interpretation_gap.claimed: The abstract and conclusion say that effects on heart rate and subjective variables were lower than expected given the concentrations achieved, 'suggesting a possible tolerance phenomenon', and that blood-pressure and temperature effects were in the expected range. The data support the contrast between measures that tracked concentration and measures that did not; 'lower than expected' remains a judgement against dose proportionality rather than against a fitted concentration-effect curve, and the authors list three alternatives themselves: scale ceilings, ceiling effects in pupil diameter and heart rate, and the fact that the second dose was given while the first dose's effects were still present.

timeline.event: The same group, two 100 mg doses 24 hours apart: exposure 77% higher after the second dose, with pupil, Maddox-wing, amphetamine-subscale and prolactin responses unchanged
The same group, two 100 mg doses 4 hours apart (Farre et al., 2015): peak concentrations roughly doubled while the two effect-time profiles were very similar
An independent group, 60 mg booster 2 hours after 120 mg: 1.5-fold higher peak concentration, effects about an hour longer, peak effects unchanged

replication.where_it_stands: The pattern of more-than-proportional concentrations with less-than-proportional effects after a second dose has now been seen at 2, 4 and 24 hours by this group and, with a booster design, by an independent Swiss group. The specific 50-then-100 mg comparison rests on this study alone.

funding.funder: Grants from the Generalitat de Catalunya (2001SGR00407, 2005SGR00032, 2009SGR718) and the Fondo de Investigacion Sanitaria (98/0181 and 01/1336) (p. 892).
funding.declared_conflicts: Not reported: the article carries no conflict-of-interest statement.
funding.affiliations_note: IMIM-Hospital del Mar and two Barcelona universities, the same group and partly the same authors as Farre et al. (2004); the two studies are not independent of each other.

what_would_settle_it: A repeated-dose study using the same dose twice at the intervals people actually redose, with a placebo-only session so that each dose can be compared with placebo, a fitted concentration-effect model for each measure, scales that do not reach ceiling, and both sexes, so that a shift of the concentration-response curve can be measured rather than inferred.

domains.domain: Randomization process (order of the two sessions)
domains.note: Described as randomized and crossover, but sequence generation and allocation concealment are not described and no period effect is reported.
Two weeks between sessions, which is far longer than the drug's half-life of about 10 hours.

Double-blind in form, but in the repeated-dose session the 50 mg dose produced measurable effects and concentrations (84.71 ng/mL) before the second capsule, so experienced participants could tell the two sessions apart, and the main outcomes are self-rated.
All ten men completed both sessions, with no missing data reported.

Cardiovascular measures, temperature, pupil diameter and plasma concentrations are objective; the subjective scales that carry the tolerance interpretation are self-rated, and the authors report ceiling effects on several.

No protocol; about forty outcomes each tested three ways without correction; Table 1 lists only variables that reached significance somewhere, so the wanted subjective effects appear only as a null statement; and both tables and figures contain mislabelling (see reporting issues).

risk_of_bias.reasoning: The design is a proper within-person double-blind crossover with objective pharmacokinetics, and the metabolic finding is clear and consistent with the group's earlier work. The overall judgment is set by the blinding, which cannot hold once the first dose is felt, and by reporting: the key subjective null results are not tabulated, the significance markers rest on many uncorrected tests, and at least three labels in the tables and figures are wrong. The source can be cited for the concentration and metabolite findings at a 2-hour interval, for blood pressure, temperature and pupil diameter rising with the added dose, and for heart rate and the wanted subjective effects not rising; it cannot be cited for the size of any tolerance, for equal repeated doses, or for women.

key_findings.finding: Adding 50 mg two hours before a 100 mg dose raised peak MDMA concentration from 202.92 ng/mL (SD 30.30) to 311.16 (SD 66.48), p<0.001, and exposure from 2 to 50 hours from 2890.73 to 4426.60 microgram.h/L, with no change in half-life (10.41 h, SD 3.55, against 10.48, SD 2.12), time to peak, volume of distribution or clearance.
key_findings.locator: Table 2, MDMA rows; Results > Pharmacokinetics, 1st-2nd paragraphs (p. 889)

key_findings.finding: The rise was greater than dose proportionality predicts: peak concentration was 12.8% and exposure 16.2% above the expected values obtained by fitting the plasma concentrations to a one-compartment model, while the metabolite HMMA was 38.2% lower at peak and 29.8% lower in exposure than proportionality predicts, and all metabolic ratios fell significantly except MDA to MDMA.

Blood pressure was higher in the repeated-dose condition on the area under the curve but not at the peak: systolic peak 29.50 (SD 9.69) against 33.30 (SD 4.13) mm Hg, not significant, with the area under the curve 49.35 (SD 24.28) against 72.96 (SD 22.12), p=0.029; diastolic peak 11.85 (SD 13.83) against 18.90 (SD 12.33), not significant, area under the curve 18.81 (SD 21.09) against 46.82 (SD 27.82), p=0.015. Every one of the ten men reached blood pressure above 140/90 mm Hg.
key_findings.locator: Table 1, SBP and DBP rows (p. 887); Results > Physiological measures, 1st paragraph (p. 888)

key_findings.finding: Heart rate did not rise with the extra dose: peak 33.50 beats/min (SD 11.87) against 33.05 (SD 13.25) and area under the curve 57.75 (SD 30.11) against 69.98 (SD 40.02), neither significant, with differences only at two scattered time points (2.3 and 5 hours, p=0.004 for the time course).
key_findings.locator: Table 1, HR rows (p. 887); Results > Physiological measures, 1st paragraph (p. 888)

key_findings.finding: Temperature and pupil diameter rose modestly: peak temperature change 0.20 degrees Celsius (SD 0.52) against 0.56 (SD 0.44) and area under the curve 0.50 against 1.61, neither significant but with significant differences at 2.3, 2.6 and 3 hours; pupil diameter peak 3.39 mm (SD 0.58) against 3.74 (SD 0.87), not significant, area under the curve 9.42 (SD 1.83) against 11.92 (SD 3.33), p=0.037. No hyperthermia occurred.
key_findings.locator: Table 1, T and PD rows (p. 887); Results > Physiological measures, 1st-2nd paragraphs (p. 888)

key_findings.finding: None of the wanted subjective effects differed significantly in peak or area under the curve between the two conditions. The only subjective differences were on the euphoria subscale (one time point), the dysphoria subscale (area under the curve and one time point), the amphetamine-like subscale (one time point) and a perceptual scale for changes in colours, which was lower in the repeated-dose condition (area under the curve 18.90, SD 22.73, against 7.70, SD 12.13; p=0.042). The sedation and stimulant subscales did not differ.
key_findings.locator: Table 1, subjective rows (p. 887); Results > Subjective effects, 1st paragraph (p. 888)

key_findings.finding: Psychomotor performance showed no difference in peak or area under the curve on any test; total reaction time was longer in the repeated-dose condition at one time point (peak increase 34.7 ms against 54.2 ms; difference at 3 hours, p=0.009).
key_findings.locator: Table 1, RT total rows (p. 887); Results > Psychomotor performance (p. 888)

key_findings.finding: The modelling attributes 0.30 (SD 0.01) of total MDMA exposure in the repeated-dose session to the 50 mg dose and 0.67 (SD 0.13) to the 100 mg dose; before the second capsule, the 50 mg dose had produced a peak of 84.71 ng/mL with 79.92 ng/mL still present at 2 hours.
key_findings.locator: Table 2, contribution rows; Results > Pharmacokinetics, 1st paragraph (p. 889)

key_findings.finding: No serious adverse reactions, hyperthermia, moderate or severe hypertension, tachycardia, hallucinations or psychotic episodes occurred, and no participant required specific treatment.

reporting_issues.issue: Table 2 prints the area under the curve from time 0 to the last measured concentration for the repeated-dose condition as 446.88 microgram.h/L, which is impossible beside that condition's own exposure from 2 to 50 hours (4426.60), its exposure to infinity (4781.13) and the same figure in Table 3 (4460.88, with the identical standard deviation of 958.90).
reporting_issues.consequence: A digit is lost in Table 2; Table 3's value of 4460.88 is the correct one, and anyone quoting Table 2 for this parameter would understate exposure tenfold.

reporting_issues.issue: In Table 3 the rows labelled HMMA and HMA carry values that fit the opposite labels: HMMA is printed as 129.20 microgram.h/L and HMA as 2365.09, while Figure 2 shows the HMMA curve peaking near 160 ng/mL and the fourth panel near 5 ng/mL, and the text treats HMMA as the main metabolite of the inhibited enzyme pathway. The printed sums are consistent either way, since HMMA plus HMA is 2494.29 in both readings.
reporting_issues.consequence: The two metabolite rows appear to be transposed; a claim about either metabolite's absolute exposure should not be taken from Table 3 without the figure.

reporting_issues.issue: Both lower panels of Figure 2 are labelled HMMA, although the legend states that the panels show MDA, HMMA and HMA; the two panels differ by a factor of about thirty in scale.
reporting_issues.consequence: The fourth panel is HMA mislabelled; the mislabelling is what makes the transposition in Table 3 detectable.

reporting_issues.issue: The statistical-analysis section names the conditions as 'M100 or M150' and the post-hoc comparison as 'M100 vs. M50+150', although the abbreviation list and every table define the repeated condition as M50+100, a total of 150 mg.
reporting_issues.consequence: The labels in the methods do not match the conditions actually given; a reader could take M150 to be a single 150 mg dose.

reporting_issues.issue: The legend of Table 3 attributes its p values to analysis of variance, while the statistical-analysis section states that pharmacokinetic parameters and metabolic ratios were compared by paired t test (and time to peak by a rank test).
reporting_issues.consequence: The test behind the metabolite comparisons cannot be determined from the paper.

reporting_issues.issue: The sample is described as ten men, but the reported proportions of previous drug use are 83.3%, 75%, 25% and 50%, which correspond to fractions of twelve rather than ten (83.3% is 10 of 12).
reporting_issues.consequence: The drug-history percentages appear to include the two men from the pilot condition whose data are otherwise not shown; the proportions should not be read as applying to the ten analysed participants.

reporting_issues.issue: In Table 1, the perceptual scale for changes in colours has a significant analysis-of-variance result for the time course (p=0.044) with the time-point entry printed as 'none'.
reporting_issues.consequence: A significant overall test with no significant time point; the finding should not be reported as a difference at any particular time.

reporting_issues.issue: There is no placebo-only session, so every effect reported in the 2-6 hour window is a comparison between two active conditions.
reporting_issues.consequence: The study measures what the extra 50 mg adds, not what MDMA does against placebo; the absolute effect sizes in Table 1 are changes from a pre-drug baseline without a placebo correction for time of day, meals and fatigue.

verification.source_read: PDF pp. 883-893 (PDFs/MDMA/Peiro_2012_RepeatedDoses2hApart.pdf), full text; Tables 1-3 were read in the extracted text and checked cell by cell against rendered images of pages 887, 889 and 890, and Figure 2's panel labels were checked on the rendered page 890.
